question: A, B, and C can complete a certain task in 20, 30, and 60 days, respectively. How many days will it take for A to finish the work if he receives help from B and C every third day?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(20, 30, 60) = 60 units.

Efficiencies: A = 60 ÷ 20 = 3, B = 60 ÷ 30 = 2, C = 60 ÷ 60 = 1.

Pattern: A works for 2 days, and A + B + C work on the 3rd day.

Work done in 3 days = (3) + (3) + (3 + 2 + 1) = 3 + 3 + 6 = 12 units.

Number of 3-day cycles needed = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 cycles.

Total time = 5 × 3 = 15 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 20 days

Time taken by B = 30 days

Time taken by C = 60 days

**Calculations:**

Let the Total Work be the LCM of the given days.

⇒ Work done by A on the 1st day = 3 units

⇒ Work done by A on the 2nd day = 3 units

⇒ Work done by A, B, and C together on the 3rd day = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 units

⇒ Total work done in one 3-day cycle = 3 + 3 + 6 = 12 units

⇒ Number of cycles required to complete 60 units of work = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 cycles

⇒ Total days required = 5 cycles × 3 days/cycle = 15 days

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Rule

Total Work is often considered as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the days taken by different individuals to complete the given task.

Work Efficiency

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Total Days. It represents the units of work done by a person in a single day.

Alternate Day Work

When people work in a specific periodic pattern, sum their combined work into a cycle and find the total time by finding the number of full cycles needed.

Combined Efficiency

When individuals work together on any given day, their combined efficiency is simply the sum of their individual daily efficiencies.
